grammarNotes.u1: Four Tones & Basic Greetings: Mandarin uses four main tones (ā, á, ǎ, à) plus a neutral tone, and tone changes meaning. Word order is Subject-Verb-Object (SVO), and yes/no questions simply add 吗 (ma) at the end.
grammarNotes.u2: Pronouns, 是 (shì) & Possession with 的 (de): Mandarin verbs do not conjugate for person or tense. Use 是 to link nouns (他是我的哥哥) and 的 to show possession (我的妈妈 = my mother), though 的 is often omitted with close relatives.
grammarNotes.u3: Numbers, Measure Words (量词) & Time Order: Numbers before nouns require a measure word such as 个 (general), 杯 (cups), 张 (flat tickets), or 本 (books). Time expressions always go before the verb (明天我们去参观博物馆).
grammarNotes.u4: Dining, Adjectives & 很 (hěn): Adjectives act like predicates without 是—use 很 (very / default linker) before them (这道菜非常好吃). Express polite requests with 请问 (may I ask) and 可以...吗 (may I...?).
grammarNotes.u5: Locations with 在 (zài), Colors & Daily Verbs: Use 在 + place + 上/里 to indicate location (把钥匙放在桌子上). Basic verbs like 去 (go), 来 (come), 吃 (eat), 喝 (drink), and 睡 (sleep) stay invariant across all subjects.
grammarNotes.u6: Directions, Transport & Preposition 往/向: Express means of transport before the verb (坐火车 = by train, 坐公交车 = by bus). Give directions with 往左转 (turn left), 直走 (walk straight), and ask locations with 在哪里.
grammarNotes.u7: Shopping, Comparisons & Money: Ask prices with 多少钱 (how much?) and express desire with 想 (want to, e.g., 我想买一件暖和的外套). Use 太...了 to express 'too...' (太贵了 = too expensive).
grammarNotes.u8: Weather, Seasons & Aspect Particle 了 (le): Indicate completed action or change of state with 了 (下雪了, 花都开了). Seasonal time phrases appear at the beginning of the sentence or right after the subject.
grammarNotes.u9: Health, Body & Giving Advice with 应该: Describe symptoms directly with 疼/痛 (头疼 = headache, 肚子疼 = stomachache) or 发烧 (have a fever). Use 应该 (should) and 记得 (remember to) for health guidance.
grammarNotes.u10: Work, Study & Frequency Adverbs: Place locations of action before the verb using 在 (她在大学学习工程学). Discuss habits and hobbies with 喜欢 (like), 热爱 (love), and time durations placed after the verb.
grammarNotes.u11: Expressing Opinions, Feelings & 觉得/认为: Introduce viewpoints with 我觉得 (I feel/think) or 我认为 (I believe). Link adjectives and nouns with 的, and express possibility with 只要...就... (as long as... then...).
grammarNotes.u12: Experiences with 过 (guò) & Relative Clauses: Mark past life experiences with 过 after the verb and ongoing/completed events with 了. Modifiers—even entire clauses—always precede 的 and the head noun.
grammarNotes.u13: Modern Tech Vocabulary & 把 (bǎ) Sentences: Mandarin creates transparent tech compounds (电脑 = electric brain, 密码 = secret code). Use 把 to bring a specific object before the verb when emphasizing how it is handled.
grammarNotes.u14: Culture, Heritage & Passive 被 (bèi) Constructions: Express passive voice with 被 (被传唱 = has been sung) or implicit passives without 被 when the subject is clearly acted upon. Cultural compounds pair classical roots cleanly.
grammarNotes.u15: Paired Conjunctions & Logical Connectors: Mandarin strongly favors paired conjunctions: 因为...所以... (because... therefore...), 虽然...但是... (although... yet...), and 如果...就... (if... then...).
grammarNotes.u16: Business Chinese & Formal Disyllabic Verbs: Professional Mandarin favors crisp two-character compounds (战略, 预算, 谈判, 妥协) and formal prepositions like 在...之前 (prior to) and 本着 (in the spirit of).
grammarNotes.u17: Scientific Register & Nominalized Structures: Academic Chinese uses precise technical terms (实验, 证据, 算法, 精密) and structures like 通过...来... (by means of...) and 表明 (demonstrates) to build objective arguments.
grammarNotes.u18: Environment, Sustainability & Causative 使/让: Discuss ecological impact with 使 (cause/enable), 有助于 (helps to), and 与...和谐共处 (live in harmony with...). Note how 保护 and 恢复 drive active policy statements.
grammarNotes.u19: Civic, Legal & Governance Discourse: Legal and institutional prose employs formal verbs like 保障 (safeguard), 维护 (uphold), and 促进 (promote), along with concise four-character phrases such as 法律面前人人平等.
grammarNotes.u20: Critical Thinking, Analysis & Rhetorical Contrast: Frame debates using 从...的角度 (from the perspective of), 尽管如此 (nevertheless), and 立足于 (grounded in) to weigh assumptions, criteria, and conclusions.
grammarNotes.u21: Literary Criticism, Aesthetics & Evocative Compounds: Aesthetic prose relies on rich literary compounds (隐喻, 象征意义, 共鸣, 崇高) and poetic four-character modifiers that compress vivid imagery into balanced rhythm.
grammarNotes.u22: Philosophy, Ethics & Abstract Discourse: Philosophical Chinese balances classical conciseness with modern rigor—pairing concepts like 无常 (impermanence), 良知 (conscience), and 内省 (introspection) with reflective structures.
grammarNotes.u23: Chengyu (成语) & Traditional Proverbs (谚语): Four-character idioms (成语) like 熟能生巧, 一针见血, 塞翁失马, and 轻而易举 condense centuries of history and folklore into razor-sharp everyday and formal speech.
grammarNotes.u24: Diplomatic, Legal & Academic Written Style (书面语): High-register Mandarin uses classical connectors such as 尽管 (notwithstanding), 因此/从而 (consequently), 此外 (furthermore), 鉴于 (in light of), and 恕我直言 (with due respect).
grammarNotes.u25: Nuance, Rhetoric & Native C2 Mastery: Achieve native elegance with idiomatic set phrases (毫无疑问, 同理, 综合来看, 经得起时间的考验), symmetrical rhythm, and effortless switching between spoken warmth and literary precision.
